text.paragraph: Four-month review, six weeks after the first ocrelizumab doses: infusion tolerance, infections, blood counts, vitamin D, heat and mood. [S]

Ms. Jordan returns six weeks after her second ocrelizumab half-dose. During the first infusion she had a scratchy throat that settled when the infusion was slowed; the second infusion went without a reaction. She has had no infections, cold sores, or diarrhea. Physical therapy started four weeks ago through a second provider, after the first service could not offer a date; she has had six sessions and does her home program most days, and she now uses a rollator at home for longer distances. Summer has brought heat sensitivity: her legs feel heavier on hot afternoons and recover when she cools down, and she has started using a cooling vest. She gets up once a night or less. Her mood is steady. [S]

tr.td: Spastic gait with a cane, as before; modified Ashworth 1+ in both legs; EDSS 6.0; timed 25-foot walk 11.1 seconds

Multiple sclerosis diagnosed elsewhere, by her account, with records of the original evaluation not available: slowly worsening walking over the past few years, leg stiffness, fatigue, urinary urgency and heat sensitivity; uses a cane; course to be classified after MRI of the brain and spine
S — Synthetic presenting picture at intake, superseded by the classified diagnosis at the consultation; the cane and a diagnosis around the time she left Congress are from public accounts.

Active primary progressive multiple sclerosis: gradual worsening of walking over more than a year without relapses, with brain lesions in periventricular, juxtacortical and infratentorial regions, three spinal cord lesions, and one gadolinium-enhancing lesion; fulfils the 1971 McDonald criteria for primary progressive disease; EDSS 6.0; synthetic modern detail linked to her publicly reported multiple sclerosis

Active primary progressive multiple sclerosis (G35.B1). Ocrelizumab started, with a mild first-infusion reaction only. White cells 5.9, lymphocytes 1.4, hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL, platelets 248; CD19 B cells 3 per microliter, depleted as expected; ALT 20 U/L. Disability stable. The heat-related heaviness is pseudo-relapse, not new disease activity. [S]
